Dwarf satellites experience impulsive expansion from gas loss followed by secular expansion from tidal stripping of their cored dark matter halos, whereas bright satellites are baryon-dominated and shrink due to centrally concentrated star formation, also acquiring ~0.2 dex higher stellar metallicities.
AI.conclusion: The distinct evolutionary pathways of dwarf and bright satellites produce identifiable features in mass-size-metallicity relations that can be compared with and tested against observations.

title: Cross-simulator transfer with foundation model summaries: Towards robust SKA-era reionization inference
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, prepared for submission to A&A
summary: Simulation-based inference (SBI) for parameter estimation is vulnerable to model misspecification: neural summaries and density estimators trained on a specific forward model typically fail when applied to data drawn from another model, or from real observations, and no training simulator can capture the full observational pipeline of a real measurement exactly. We show that a self-supervised Vision Transformer (ViT), pretrained label-free on a fast approximate simulator, produces transferable data summaries that generalize across simulators. Without retraining, it can be reused as a frozen encoder to infer astrophysical parameters from a completely different simulator that resolves the radiative transfer explicitly, on which it has never seen either data or parameters. As a concrete use case in 21cm cosmology, SKATR, a ViT pretrained with a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), serves as a foundation model for reionization inference from upcoming SKA measurements: SKATR is pretrained once on 67k low-cost, noiseless semi-numerical 21cmFAST lightcones, then frozen and applied to hydrodynamical Loreli II lightcones, where a lightweight conditional flow matching head infers five astrophysical parameters; the encoder is never shown Loreli data, its parameters, or any noise. In our comparison, SKATR yields the most precise and best-calibrated posteriors across all five parameters, matching the accuracy of the fully-supervised in-domain baseline while requiring 2.6x fewer radiative-transfer simulations. Under realistic SKA AA* noise, only SKATR remains simultaneously accurate, informative, and calibrated, outperforming even a supervised baseline retrained from scratch on noisy data. Self-supervised pretraining on computationally efficient semi-numerical simulations is therefore a viable route to calibrated, simulator- and noise-agnostic reionization inference for the SKA-era.

AI.tldr: A self-supervised Vision Transformer (SKATR), pretrained label-free on fast approximate 21cmFAST simulations using a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture, produces transferable data summaries that generalize to a completely different, more expensive radiative-transfer simulator (Loreli II) without retraining. When frozen as an encoder and paired with a lightweight conditional flow-matching head, SKATR infers five astrophysical parameters more precisely and with better calibration than supervised baselines, especially under realistic SKA noise, while requiring 2.6x fewer expensive simulations.
AI.motivation: Simulation-based inference for parameter estimation is highly vulnerable to model misspecification: neural summaries and density estimators trained on one forward model fail on data from other models or real observations, since no simulator perfectly captures the real measurement pipeline.
AI.method: Pretrain a Vision Transformer with a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) in a self-supervised, label-free manner on 67k low-cost, noiseless semi-numerical 21cmFAST lightcones. The frozen encoder is then applied to hydrodynamical Loreli II lightcones it has never seen, paired with a lightweight conditional flow-matching head to infer five astrophysical parameters.
AI.result: SKATR yields the most precise and best-calibrated posteriors across all five parameters, matching the accuracy of a fully-supervised in-domain baseline while requiring 2.6x fewer radiative-transfer simulations. Under realistic SKA AA* noise, only SKATR remains accurate, informative, and calibrated, outperforming even a supervised baseline retrained from scratch on noisy data.
AI.conclusion: Self-supervised pretraining on computationally efficient semi-numerical simulations is a viable route to calibrated, simulator- and noise-agnostic reionization inference for the SKA era.

title: Phase-Space Diagnostics for Dwarf Galaxies in Cluster Environments
comment: 17 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to ApJ, comments are welcome
summary: Ongoing effort is devoted to observing spectroscopic samples of dwarf galaxies in clusters, allowing the analysis of their distribution and associated trends in projected phase-space (PPS), i.e. line-of-sight velocity vs. projected clustercentric distance. By utilizing the resolved baryonic halos inside the galaxy clusters of a cosmological simulation from the Magneticum suite, we complement on prior studies with dedicated focus on the dwarf galaxy population ($M_\ast<10^9\,M_\odot$) and correlations between infall time and location in PPS. The inferred trend recovers the radial correlation reported by prior works, but we find a significant fraction ($\geq30\%$) of recently accreted galaxies at locations that were previously predicted to be dominated by ancient infallers. Splitting the diagram with an infall time threshold of 3 Gyr, we develop a detailed infall time template in PPS. We provide our data to allow observers to statistically infer the time of infall of their sample when placing them on the PPS. Additionally, we review the trajectories in PPS of different orbits and their dependence on the observer's orientation. Compared to massive galaxies, we find a much broader radial distribution for dwarfs in 3D PS. Utilizing a set of high-resolution idealized simulations, we predict strongly altered orbits for dark matter-deficient galaxies.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes dwarf galaxies in cluster projected phase-space (PPS) using the Magneticum cosmological simulation, finding that a significant fraction (≥30%) of recently accreted dwarfs occupy PPS regions previously thought to be dominated by ancient infallers. The authors develop an infall time template with a 3 Gyr threshold, provide data for observers to statistically infer infall times, and examine how orbital trajectories in PPS depend on observer orientation. They also show dwarfs have broader radial distributions in 3D phase-space than massive galaxies, and that dark matter-deficient galaxies have strongly altered orbits.
AI.motivation: To extend prior PPS studies focused on massive galaxies to the dwarf galaxy population (M*<10^9 Msun), and to provide a framework and template enabling observers to statistically infer infall times of dwarf galaxies in clusters from their PPS positions.
AI.method: Utilizes the cosmological hydrodynamic simulation Magneticum to analyze resolved baryonic halos of dwarf galaxies in clusters. Constructs PPS diagrams (line-of-sight velocity vs. projected clustercentric distance), correlates infall time with PPS location, and uses a 3 Gyr infall time threshold to build a template. Additionally employs high-resolution idealized simulations to study orbits of dark matter-deficient galaxies and their orientation dependence in PPS.
AI.result: Recovers the radial correlation between infall time and PPS location from prior work, but finds ≥30% of recently accreted galaxies at PPS locations previously predicted to be dominated by ancient infallers. Dwarfs show much broader radial distributions in 3D phase-space compared to massive galaxies. Dark matter-deficient galaxies are predicted to have strongly altered orbits in idealized simulations.
AI.conclusion: The PPS-infall time relation for dwarf galaxies is more complex than previously thought, with significant contamination of recent infallers in ancient-dominated regions. The provided infall time template and data enable observers to statistically infer infall epochs of dwarf galaxies, while highlighting the need to account for orbital alterations in dark matter-deficient systems.

title: Revisiting the Hubble tension with an inverse power-law early dark energy
summary: We propose a new early dark energy with a potential that has an inverse power-law asymptotic tail to alleviate the Hubble tension. Fitting this model to the datasets of CMB+BAO+SN+H0DN, one obtains a 68$\%$ confidence-level value of $H_0\sim 70.20^{+0.60}_{-0.47}$ km s$^{-1}$Mpc$^{-1}$ and a best-fit value of $H_0\sim 70.56$ km s$^{-1}$Mpc$^{-1}$ for index $n=10$. We show that this model can be tested by future data of CMB and matter power spectra. Finally, we briefly discuss fine-tuning problems related to this model.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a new early dark energy model with an inverse power-law asymptotic tail potential to alleviate the Hubble tension. Fitting to CMB+BAO+SN+H0DN data yields H0 ~ 70.20 km/s/Mpc (68% CL) and best-fit 70.56 km/s/Mpc for index n=10, with potential testing via future CMB and matter power spectra data, plus a discussion of fine-tuning issues.
AI.motivation: To address the Hubble tension—the discrepancy between early and late universe measurements of the Hubble constant—by proposing a new early dark energy model with an inverse power-law asymptotic tail potential.
AI.method: A new early dark energy model featuring a potential with an inverse power-law asymptotic tail is proposed and fitted to combined cosmological datasets (CMB, BAO, SN, and H0DN). The model is evaluated for index n=10, and its testability is assessed through future CMB and matter power spectrum observations.
AI.result: The fit yields H0 = 70.20^{+0.60}_{-0.47} km/s/Mpc at 68% confidence level, with a best-fit value of 70.56 km/s/Mpc for index n=10, substantially alleviating the Hubble tension. The model is shown to be distinguishable by future CMB and matter power spectrum data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed early dark energy model with an inverse power-law asymptotic tail effectively alleviates the Hubble tension, is testable with upcoming CMB and matter power spectrum observations, though fine-tuning issues associated with the model require careful consideration.

title: COSMOS-Web: From early star-formation enhancement to late suppression in galaxy groups
summary: Galaxy groups trace dense environments where interactions, gas removal, and reduced accretion may drive quenching. Common diagnostics trace star formation over short timescales ($\lesssim 100$ Myr), so time-resolved star formation histories (SFHs) are needed to separate brief changes from longer-term evolution at fixed mass and redshift. Using COSMOS-Web data, we test how group environment correlates with star formation, how this evolves with cosmic time and group-centric distance, and how high-richness group galaxies differ from field galaxies. We combine COSMOS2025/COSMOS-Web stellar masses and non-parametric SFHs with AMICO group detections and probabilistic memberships. Using stacked SFHs and evolution diagnostics, we compare group and matched field galaxies as a function of normalized group-centric distance ($R_{\rm norm}$), using the richest groups as reference. The clearest suppression appears at $z<1.5$ and low-to-intermediate mass ($8.1<\log(M_\star/M_\odot)<10.5$), reaching a group-field SFH deficit up to 0.8 dex. At $z>1.5$, SFHs show weak suppression or occasional enhancement, a more heterogeneous contrast despite possible systematics. The radial signal also evolves: low-redshift profiles are broadly quenching-oriented across radius, while a clear inner-outer contrast emerges at $z\gtrsim 1$, though ordering at $z\gtrsim 2$ remains tentative given growing uncertainty in AMICO centroids. These results suggest an evolving picture: at early epochs groups are more mixed, with both suppressed and elevated SFHs; from $z\lesssim 1.5$, suppression dominates, most clearly for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies. This fits inner-region galaxies spending more time within the group potential, undergoing more passages through dense intra-group regions, and receiving less pristine cold gas, making quenching progressively clearer with cosmic time.

AI.tldr: Using COSMOS-Web data, stacked non-parametric star formation histories (SFHs), and AMICO group detections, this study examines how group environment affects star formation as a function of mass, redshift, and group-centric distance. Suppression is clearest at z<1.5 for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies (deficit up to 0.8 dex), while at z>1.5 the signal is heterogeneous. Radial profiles show broad quenching at low z but an inner-outer contrast emerges at z≳1, suggesting group quenching becomes progressively established with cosmic time.
AI.motivation: Standard star formation diagnostics only probe short timescales (<100 Myr), preventing the separation of transient changes from long-term evolution. Time-resolved SFHs are needed to understand how group environments drive quenching across cosmic time, at fixed mass and redshift.
AI.method: The study combines COSMOS2025/COSMOS-Web stellar masses and non-parametric SFHs with AMICO group detections and probabilistic memberships. Stacked SFHs and evolution diagnostics are used to compare group galaxies to matched field galaxies as a function of normalized group-centric distance (R_norm), using the richest groups as reference.
AI.result: The clearest star formation suppression occurs at z<1.5 for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies (8.1<log M_star/M_sun<10.5), with group-field SFH deficits up to 0.8 dex. At z>1.5, suppression is weak or sometimes reversed (enhancement). Radial profiles evolve: low-redshift groups are broadly quenching across radius, while inner-outer contrast emerges at z≳1; ordering at z≳2 is tentative due to AMICO centroid uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: The picture of environmental quenching in groups is evolving: at early epochs, groups are more heterogeneous with both suppressed and elevated SFHs; from z≲1.5, suppression dominates, particularly for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies. This is consistent with inner-region galaxies spending more time in the group potential, undergoing more passages through dense intra-group regions, and receiving less pristine cold gas, making quenching progressively clearer with cosmic time.

title: Approximating the peculiar velocity distribution of dark matter halos with Tsallis statistics
summary: Dark matter halos, which host galaxies and galaxy clusters, have peculiar velocities far from thermal equilibrium. Characterizing the nonlinear and non-Gaussian features of this velocity distribution improves our understanding of the gravitational evolution of the cosmic web and supports related cosmological applications. We endeavor to establish a connection between the peculiar velocity distribution of halos and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, with the objective of obtaining a model that is both concise and accurate for practical applications. We extracted halo samples from large N-body simulations and performed maximum-likelihood fits to the peculiar velocity distributions using a two-parameter Tsallis model, derived from non-extensive statistical mechanics. On the theoretical side, we reformulated the halo distribution in the superstatistics framework by means of a generalized Gram-Charlier expansion based on the gamma distribution. For halo peculiar velocities below 1000 km/s, the Tsallis model achieves 5 percent accuracy over z=0-2, with performance improving toward lower redshifts. Our results show that the halo velocity distribution becomes increasingly non-Gaussian and departs further from equilibrium over time. The best-fit parameters depend only weakly on mass, though low-mass halos exhibit slightly stronger non-Gaussianity. The two parameters, especially the velocity dispersion, offer promising probes of cosmological parameters. Theoretically, we find that in general the halo peculiar velocity distribution function is expressible as a superposition of a series of Tsallis distribution functions, while simulation results demonstrate that the zeroth-order approximation, namely a single Tsallis function, already achieves sufficient accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper connects the peculiar velocity distribution of dark matter halos to nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, demonstrating that a two-parameter Tsallis model fits halo velocity distributions with 5% accuracy for velocities below 1000 km/s across z=0-2. The work reveals that halo velocity distributions become increasingly non-Gaussian over time, and theoretically reformulates the distribution using a generalized Gram-Charlier expansion in the superstatistics framework, showing that the distribution can be expressed as a superposition of Tsallis functions with the zeroth-order single-Tsallis approximation being sufficient for practical accuracy.
AI.motivation: Dark matter halos exhibit peculiar velocities far from thermal equilibrium, and characterizing their nonlinear and non-Gaussian velocity distributions is important for understanding gravitational evolution of the cosmic web and for cosmological applications. The authors seek a concise yet accurate model connecting halo velocity distributions to nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
AI.method: The authors extracted halo samples from large N-body simulations and performed maximum-likelihood fits to peculiar velocity distributions using a two-parameter Tsallis model from non-extensive statistical mechanics. Theoretically, they reformulated the halo distribution within the superstatistics framework using a generalized Gram-Charlier expansion based on the gamma distribution.
AI.result: For halo peculiar velocities below 1000 km/s, the Tsallis model achieves 5% accuracy over z=0-2, performing better at lower redshifts. The halo velocity distribution becomes increasingly non-Gaussian and departs further from equilibrium over time. Best-fit parameters depend only weakly on mass, though low-mass halos show slightly stronger non-Gaussianity. The two parameters, especially velocity dispersion, offer promising probes of cosmological parameters. Theoretically, the halo peculiar velocity distribution function is expressible as a superposition of Tsallis distribution functions, and the zeroth-order single-Tsallis approximation already achieves sufficient accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The Tsallis model provides a concise and accurate description of halo peculiar velocity distributions across cosmic time, bridging nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with cosmological structure formation. The velocity dispersion parameter serves as a promising cosmological probe, and the superstatistics framework offers a theoretically grounded foundation for this empirical fit.

title: Systematic uncertainties on DESI Tully-Fisher distances constrained with Integral Field Spectroscopy
summary:
The Tully--Fisher (TF) relation is an empirical tool for estimating distances to spiral galaxies. The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Peculiar Velocity (PV) Survey uses \texttt{`tractor'} photometric position angles to place fibers along the galaxy's semi-major axis and infer maximum rotational velocities for $\approx$ 53,000 spirals. Systematic errors arise if the photometric PA differs from the kinematic PA from velocity fields.
  We quantify systematic uncertainties in DESI-TF distance estimates from photometric PAs and assess the impact of photometric--kinematic PA misalignments.
  We analyze 215 nearby galaxies from the PISCO and AMUSING surveys, estimating maximum rotational velocities at $0.4\,R_{26}$ for consistency with DESI-PV. Kinematic parameters are derived using \texttt{`PaFit'} from \texttt{`Cappellari Software'}. Global photometric parameters rely on Siena Galaxy Atlas SGA-2020 \texttt{`tractor'} data, with \texttt{`HostPhot'} as an alternative approach.
  Approximately $28\%$ of our sample exhibit photometric--kinematic PA misalignments $>10^\circ$. The median bias in distance is $\approx +1.98\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ with a skewed residual distribution of outliers. The overall distance standard deviation is $19.35\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, with misaligned galaxies showing twice the dispersion of aligned ones. The Mean Percentage Error is $2.8\% \pm 1.96$ (SE).
  High galaxy-to-galaxy scatter appears in DESI-TF distances, particularly for misaligned systems. Because DESI-TF targets lack kinematic PA measurements, we recommend a global fractional uncertainty of $\approx 3.5\%$. When kinematic information is available, aligned galaxies with offsets $<10^\circ$ are consistent with $\approx 1\%$ uncertainty, while strongly misaligned or incomplete systems warrant an upper threshold of $\approx 10\%$.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies systematic uncertainties in DESI-TF distance estimates arising from photometric-kinematic position angle (PA) misalignments. Analyzing 215 nearby galaxies, ~28% show PA misalignments >10°, leading to a median distance bias of ~+1.98 Mpc and an overall distance standard deviation of 19.35 Mpc. The authors recommend a global fractional uncertainty of ~3.5% for DESI-TF targets, ~1% for well-aligned galaxies with kinematic information, and up to ~10% for strongly misaligned systems.
AI.motivation: The Tully-Fisher relation is a key empirical tool for estimating distances to spiral galaxies, but the DESI Peculiar Velocity Survey relies on photometric position angles to place fibers and infer rotational velocities. If photometric PAs differ from kinematic PAs, systematic errors arise in distance estimates. This work aims to quantify these systematic uncertainties and assess the impact of PA misalignments on DESI-TF distance precision.
AI.method: The authors analyze 215 nearby galaxies from the PISCO and AMUSING surveys. Maximum rotational velocities are estimated at 0.4 R26 for consistency with DESI-PV. Kinematic parameters are derived using the PaFit tool from Cappellari Software, while global photometric parameters rely on Siena Galaxy Atlas SGA-2020 'tractor' data with HostPhot as an alternative approach. Photometric and kinematic PAs are compared to quantify misalignments and their effect on distance estimates.
AI.result: Approximately 28% of the sample exhibits photometric-kinematic PA misalignments >10°. The median bias in distance is approximately +1.98 Mpc with a skewed residual distribution of outliers. The overall distance standard deviation is 19.35 Mpc, with misaligned galaxies showing twice the dispersion of aligned ones. The Mean Percentage Error is 2.8% ± 1.96 (SE). High galaxy-to-galaxy scatter is observed, particularly for misaligned systems.
AI.conclusion: Given that DESI-TF targets lack kinematic PA measurements, a global fractional uncertainty of ~3.5% is recommended. When kinematic information is available, aligned galaxies with offsets <10° are consistent with ~1% uncertainty, while strongly misaligned or incomplete systems warrant an upper threshold of ~10% uncertainty. These calibrated uncertainties are essential for properly weighting DESI-TF distances in cosmological analyses.

title: ELUCID-DESI II. Revealing dark matter mass, tidal, and velocity (MTV) fields using galaxy group phase information
summary: We introduce a novel method for reconstructing the cosmic mass, tidal, and velocity (MTV) fields over the redshift range $0 < z < 0.6$ using the phase information of galaxy groups. This approach replaces the explicit theoretical bias correction typically needed to relate galaxy groups to the underlying dark matter density field with a simulation-calibrated statistical mapping, reducing a major source of systematic uncertainty and making the method directly applicable to spectroscopic redshift surveys such as the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS). We evaluate the performance of our MTV reconstruction pipeline with mock redshift surveys that include a comprehensive set of observational selection effects. The galaxy groups used as tracers are identified with an extended halo-based group finder applied to the DESI mock galaxy catalogue with an apparent magnitude limit of $m_z < 19.65$, yielding a galaxy number comparable to that of the DESI BGS faint sample ($m_r < 20.175$). Our tests show that the reconstructed velocities are accurate and unbiased, with a residual dispersion of $\sim 120\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ across the redshift bins. The recovered velocity field allows us to shift galaxy groups to their real-space positions, thereby correcting for the Kaiser effect. By iteratively applying this Kaiser correction to the galaxy groups, we further reconstruct the tidal field and the mass-density distribution. The reconstruction is stable with respect to the grid resolution. Overall, our results demonstrate that this group-based phase-space reconstruction provides a robust pathway to recovering the dark matter MTV fields, with strong prospects for application to DESI BGS data.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a novel group-based phase-space reconstruction method to recover cosmic mass, tidal, and velocity (MTV) fields over 0 < z < 0.6, using galaxy groups as tracers and a simulation-calibrated statistical mapping instead of explicit bias corrections. Evaluated with mock redshift surveys including observational selection effects, the method yields unbiased velocity reconstructions with ~120 km/s residual dispersion, enables Kaiser-effect correction, and robustly reconstructs tidal and mass-density fields, showing strong applicability to DESI BGS data.
AI.motivation: To avoid explicit theoretical bias corrections that relate galaxy groups to the dark matter density field (a major source of systematic uncertainty), and to make cosmic MTV field reconstruction directly applicable to spectroscopic redshift surveys like the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey.
AI.method: Use phase information of galaxy groups identified with an extended halo-based group finder on a DESI mock galaxy catalogue (m_z < 19.65, comparable to DESI BGS faint sample), replace explicit bias correction with a simulation-calibrated statistical mapping, reconstruct velocity fields, shift groups to real space via iterative Kaiser correction, then recover tidal and mass-density fields; all tested with mocks including comprehensive observational selection effects.
AI.result: Reconstructed velocities are accurate and unbiased with residual dispersion of ~120 km/s across redshift bins; velocity field enables Kaiser correction; iterative reconstruction yields stable tidal and mass-density fields with respect to grid resolution.
AI.conclusion: The group-based phase-space reconstruction provides a robust pathway to recovering dark matter MTV fields and holds strong prospects for application to DESI BGS data.

title: A radio continuum view of Stephan's Quintet: age, dynamics and origin of the shock
comment: 25 pages, 13 Figures, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present a detailed, multi-band radio continuum study of the compact galaxy group Stephan's Quintet (HCG 92). We use a combination of new (MeerKAT, uGMRT) and archival (LOFAR, VLA) observations covering the $\rm 120\,MHz{-}8\,GHz$ frequency range to examine the radio properties of the group, focusing on the famous radio ridge and surrounding diffuse emission. We find filamentary substructure and branching in the southern half of the ridge, confirm an extension of the ridge to the northwest, and identify for the first time a radio counterpart to the gas bridge linking the ridge and NGC 7319. The northern ridge, northwest extension and diffuse emission have relatively steep, curved spectra, with a high-frequency spectral index gradient running north-south along the ridge. We show that the ridge emission primarily arises from a single physical mechanism, probably strong ($\mathcal{M}\simeq 40-100$) shocks in cold gas, caused by the $\rm \sim850-1000\,kms^{-1}$ collision between NGC 7318B and tidal gas filaments produced by past galaxy interactions. Synchrotron spectral age estimates suggest the collision began at the north end of the ridge $\rm \sim20\,Myr$ ago, and finished only $\rm \sim5-6\,Myr$ ago in the south, with the southern end of the shocked ridge likely still within or close to the disk of NGC 7318B. Based on this age gradient, we find that the angle between the intruder galaxy's motion and the tidal filaments was probably only about 15 degrees, and combining this with the lack of a spectral index gradient in the diffuse radio emission suggests that NGC 7318B's direction of motion is probably close to the line of sight.

AI.tldr: A multi-band radio continuum study (120 MHz–8 GHz) of Stephan's Quintet using MeerKAT, uGMRT, LOFAR, and VLA data, revealing filamentary substructure in the radio ridge, a new radio counterpart to the gas bridge, and evidence that the ridge emission arises from strong shocks (Mach 40–100) caused by NGC 7318B colliding with tidal gas filaments at ~850–1000 km/s. Spectral ages indicate the collision progressed from north to south over ~20 Myr, with the intruder's motion nearly along the line of sight.
AI.motivation: To characterize the radio continuum properties of the compact galaxy group Stephan's Quintet across a broad frequency range, particularly to understand the physical mechanism behind the famous radio ridge and surrounding diffuse emission, and to constrain the geometry and timescale of the galaxy interaction.
AI.method: Combined new MeerKAT and uGMRT observations with archival LOFAR and VLA data covering 120 MHz to 8 GHz. Performed spectral index and synchrotron spectral age analyses of the ridge and diffuse emission, examining substructure, morphology, and spectral gradients to infer shock conditions and interaction geometry.
AI.result: Found filamentary substructure and branching in the southern ridge, an extension to the northwest, and a first-time radio detection of the gas bridge to NGC 7319. The ridge has steep, curved spectra with a north-south high-frequency spectral index gradient. Ridge emission is consistent with a single mechanism: strong shocks (Mach 40–100) from the ~850–1000 km/s collision of NGC 7318B with tidal gas filaments. Spectral ages show the collision began ~20 Myr ago in the north and ended ~5–6 Myr ago in the south, implying a ~15° angle between the intruder's motion and the filaments, with NGC 7318B moving nearly along the line of sight.
AI.conclusion: The radio ridge in Stephan's Quintet is produced by a strong shock event from a high-velocity galaxy collision, with the interaction progressing from north to south over roughly 15–20 Myr. The intruder galaxy's trajectory is close to the line of sight, and the diffuse emission shows no corresponding spectral gradient, consistent with this geometry.

title: Derivative hierarchy as the origin of kernel-dependent trends in Gaussian process reconstructions of the hubble parameter
summary: We perform a model independent reconstruction of the cosmic expansion history using Gaussian Process regression, investigating how the smoothness properties of covariance kernels influence the inferred Hubble parameter. Using 32 cosmic chronometer measurements, we reconstruct $H(z)$ with the Matérn $3/2$, $5/2$, $7/2$, $9/2$, and Squared Exponential kernels, which form a well-defined hierarchy of differentiability. Across this hierarchy, we observe a systematic and monotonic trend in which increasing kernel smoothness is associated with progressively lower reconstructed values of the present-day Hubble constant $H_0$, accompanied by reduced statistical uncertainties. Rather than indicating a statistical preference for a specific kernel, this behaviour reflects the sensitivity of non-parametric reconstructions to the assumed smoothness prior encoded in the covariance function. The same ordering is reflected in descriptive goodness-of-fit statistics and remains stable when incorporating recent DESI DR2 BAO measurements and performing jackknife resampling tests, demonstrating robustness against individual data points and dataset variations. Additional analysis of derivative reconstructions shows that differences in kernel differentiability propagate into the local slope of the expansion history, providing a consistent interpretation of the observed ordering in $H_0$. Our results highlight that kernel smoothness plays an important role in Gaussian Process reconstructions and should be carefully accounted for when interpreting non-parametric cosmological inferences.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a model-independent reconstruction of the cosmic expansion history using Gaussian Process regression with 32 cosmic chronometer measurements, testing five covariance kernels (Matérn 3/2 through 9/2 and Squared Exponential) that form a hierarchy of differentiability. The authors find a systematic, monotonic trend where increasing kernel smoothness yields progressively lower reconstructed H0 values with reduced uncertainties, and show this reflects the smoothness prior's influence on non-parametric reconstructions rather than statistical preference. The trend remains stable under addition of DESI DR2 BAO measurements and jackknife tests, and derivative reconstructions confirm kernel differentiability propagates into the local slope of expansion history.
AI.motivation: Gaussian Process regression is widely used for model-independent cosmological reconstructions, but the choice of covariance kernel—which encodes assumptions about smoothness—may significantly influence inferred parameters like H0. The authors aim to systematically investigate how kernel smoothness properties propagate into reconstructed cosmological quantities.
AI.method: Using 32 cosmic chronometer measurements, the authors reconstruct H(z) via Gaussian Process regression with a hierarchy of covariance kernels (Matérn 3/2, 5/2, 7/2, 9/2, and Squared Exponential) ordered by differentiability. They compare reconstructed H0 values, statistical uncertainties, and goodness-of-fit statistics across kernels, and validate robustness using DESI DR2 BAO data and jackknife resampling. Derivative reconstructions are additionally analyzed to assess how kernel differentiability affects the local slope of the expansion history.
AI.result: A systematic monotonic trend is observed: increasing kernel smoothness leads to progressively lower reconstructed H0 values with reduced statistical uncertainties. This ordering persists across goodness-of-fit statistics and remains stable with DESI DR2 BAO data and jackknife tests, demonstrating robustness to dataset variations. Derivative analyses show that kernel differentiability propagates into the local slope of the expansion history, offering a consistent explanation for the H0 ordering.
AI.conclusion: Kernel smoothness plays a critical role in Gaussian Process reconstructions of cosmology. The observed H0 trend is not evidence for kernel preference but highlights the sensitivity of non-parametric reconstructions to the assumed smoothness prior. This should be carefully accounted for when interpreting non-parametric cosmological inferences.

title: Visualizing Disequilibrium: Tracing Two-Point Correlations to Specific Spatial Structures in the Milky Way
comment: Published in the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: The Two-Point Correlation Function can be used to demonstrate the existence of substructure within a dataset, but typical implementations do not track the individual points which contribute to each specific substructure. In this paper, we develop an algorithm that traces a two-point correlation signal back to the contributions of each data point, allowing for structure to be visualized in novel ways. Using this tool, we find substantial evidence for pervasive spatial clustering in the Milky Way and reveal complex undulations that warp the previously discovered vertical density waves. We also explore the ``clumping" of stars in the thick disk and near-halo regions and discuss the possibility of dating the structure.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an algorithm that traces two-point correlation function signals back to individual data point contributions, enabling novel visualization of substructure. Applied to Milky Way data, it reveals pervasive spatial clustering, complex undulations warping vertical density waves, and clumping of stars in thick disk and near-halo regions, with potential for dating these structures.
AI.motivation: Typical implementations of the Two-Point Correlation Function can demonstrate substructure within a dataset but do not track which individual points contribute to each specific substructure, limiting the ability to visualize and characterize the underlying structure in detail.
AI.method: The authors develop an algorithm that traces a two-point correlation signal back to the contributions of each individual data point, allowing the structure detected by the correlation function to be visualized in novel ways.
AI.result: Using the tool, substantial evidence for pervasive spatial clustering in the Milky Way is found. The analysis reveals complex undulations that warp previously discovered vertical density waves, and explores the "clumping" of stars in the thick disk and near-halo regions, with discussion of dating the structure.
AI.conclusion: The algorithm provides a new means of attributing two-point correlation signals to individual points, offering novel visualization of substructure and yielding new insights into Milky Way structure, including undulations in vertical density waves and clumping in the thick disk and near-halo regions, with potential implications for dating structures.

title: Bumpy inflation from explosive particle production
summary: We present a first-principles derivation of an effective inflaton potential with a bumpy feature. We consider the coupling of a spectator field χto the inflaton φsuch that χis massive enough for almost all values of φ, but becomes massless when the inflaton crossed the value φ_\star. This gives rise to a burst of χ-particle production at φ=φ_\star. By taking the backreaction of the particle production, we obtain a bumpy feature in the effective potential.

AI.tldr: The paper derives an effective inflaton potential with a bumpy feature from first principles by coupling a spectator field χ to the inflaton φ. The coupling makes χ massive for most φ values but massless at a specific point φ_⋆, causing a burst of particle production at that point, whose backreaction generates a bump in the effective inflaton potential.
AI.motivation: To provide a first-principles derivation of an effective inflaton potential containing a bumpy feature, which is relevant for cosmological observables such as primordial black hole production or features in the power spectrum.
AI.method: The approach considers a spectator field χ coupled to the inflaton φ such that χ's mass depends on φ, becoming massless at φ = φ_⋆. This triggers a burst of χ-particle production at the crossing point. The backreaction of these produced particles is then incorporated to derive the resulting bumpy modification to the effective inflaton potential.
AI.result: A first-principles derivation yields an effective inflaton potential exhibiting a bumpy feature, arising from the backreaction of spectator field particle production at the specific inflaton field value φ_⋆.
AI.conclusion: The particle production of a spectator field at a massless crossing point provides a well-motivated microscopic mechanism for generating bumpy features in the inflaton potential, which can have observable cosmological consequences.

title: SERENADE III: Insight into the Origin of the High Dust Temperature and High [O III]/[C II] Ratio at $z\gtrsim6$
summary: We present an analysis of ALMA high-frequency observations of nine bright Lyman-break galaxies at $5.8<z_{\rm spec}<8.3$. Our sample consists of five galaxies at $z\sim6$ newly observed in Band-9 and/or 10, allowing us to better constrain the dust temperature ($T_{\rm dust}$) in a statistical sample of $z\gtrsim6$ galaxies. Our measurements of the dust temperature at $z\sim6-9$ suggest most of the star-forming galaxies show $T_{\rm dust}\sim40\,{\rm K}$ on average, whereas three galaxies show significantly higher $T_{\rm dust}$ ($\gtrsim60\,{\rm K}$). We find a potential negative correlation between $T_{\rm dust}$ and gas-phase metallicity with $T_{\rm dust}\propto Z^{-0.50\pm0.19}$, implying decreased dust shielding and efficient dust heating in low-metallicity environments. Given the systematic offset of $T_{\rm dust}$ between $z\sim0$ and $z\sim6-9$ at fixed metallicity, we find $T_{\rm dust}$ is well described by sSFR as well as $Z$ with $\log T_{\rm dust}=-0.25^{+0.03}_{-0.04}\times(\log Z-0.57\times\log {\rm sSFR})+4.88^{+0.47}_{-0.43}$ across $z\sim0$ to $z\sim6-9$. Simultaneously with the dust continuum, these observations cover the [OI]63$μ$m emission line for five galaxies, which traces dense neutral gas. We find a lower [CII]/[OI] ratio in $z\gtrsim6$ galaxies than in local samples, suggesting that [CII] becomes fainter due to collisional de-excitation at high gas density. Combining the [OI], [OIII], and [CII] lines and cloudy modeling, our results imply $\log U_{\rm ion}\sim-2$ and $\log n_{\rm H}\,[{\rm cm}^{-3}]\sim2.5$ in $z\gtrsim6$ galaxies, which is $\sim3-10\times$ higher $U_{\rm ion}$ and $\sim2-3\times$ higher $n_{\rm H}$ than the local samples. The combination of these enhanced $U_{\rm ion}$ and $n_{\rm H}$ naturally explains the high [OIII]/[CII] ratio at $z\gtrsim6$.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes ALMA high-frequency observations of nine bright Lyman-break galaxies at z~6-9, measuring dust temperatures. Most galaxies show T_dust~40K, while three show significantly higher temperatures (>60K). The study finds a negative correlation between dust temperature and gas-phase metallicity, and derives a comprehensive T_dust relation dependent on both sSFR and metallicity across z~0 to z~6-9. The observations also cover [OI]63μm line for five galaxies, revealing lower [CII]/[OI] ratios at high redshift, and combined cloudy modeling implies higher ionization parameter and gas density in z>6 galaxies that naturally explains the elevated [OIII]/[CII] ratio.
AI.motivation: To better constrain the dust temperature in a statistical sample of z>6 galaxies using new ALMA Band-9/10 observations, and to understand the physical conditions (metallicity, gas density, ionization) driving dust temperature and line ratios in early galaxies.
AI.method: ALMA high-frequency (Band-9 and/or 10) observations of nine bright Lyman-break galaxies at 5.8<z_spec<8.3, including five newly observed galaxies at z~6. The analysis measures dust temperature via dust continuum, correlates with gas-phase metallicity, and combines [OI]63μm, [OIII], and [CII] line measurements with cloudy photoionization modeling to derive ionization parameter (U_ion) and hydrogen density (n_H).
AI.result: Dust temperatures at z~6-9 are ~40K on average, with three galaxies showing T_dust>60K. A negative correlation T_dust∝Z^(-0.50±0.19) is found. T_dust is described by log T_dust = -0.25× (log Z - 0.57×log sSFR) + 4.88 across z~0 to z~6-9. The [CII]/[OI] ratio is lower in z>6 galaxies than in local samples. Cloudy modeling implies log U_ion~-2 and log n_H~2.5 cm^-3 in z>6 galaxies, which are ~3-10x and ~2-3x higher than local samples, respectively.
AI.conclusion: Dust temperature in high-redshift galaxies is governed by both metallicity and specific star formation rate, with low-metallicity environments having less dust shielding and more efficient dust heating. The combination of enhanced ionization parameter and gas density at z>6 naturally explains the elevated [OIII]/[CII] ratio observed in these galaxies, pointing to higher density and more highly ionized conditions in the interstellar medium of early galaxies.

title: Near universality of nonlinear transverse and radial velocity responses in spherical collapse with arbitrary radial profiles
summary: The nonlinear relation between density and expansion is usually formulated for a homogeneous spherical top hat, which has a single local Hubble rate. A smooth spherical profile instead expands differently along ($H_{\parallel}$) and across ($H_{\perp}$) the radial direction-a direct signature of radial inhomogeneity. We show that, for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise response is nevertheless fixed by one top-hat function. Given the local density contrast $δ(t,r)$ and the enclosed contrast $Δ(t,r)$, a transverse response and its derivative determine $H_{\perp}$ and $H_{\parallel}$. The linear and second-order limits are algebraic maps whose only dynamical input is the usual growth rate $f$. An exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating an evolution equation. We check that it reconstructs full $Λ$LTB profiles to numerical precision. We also provide a derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit that requires only $f$, $δ$, and $Δ$. Across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations and for a shell located in the compensated transition, the maximum relative errors are $0.3\%$ and $0.7\%$ in the transverse and radial responses, respectively. This compact formulation separates the production of a density profile from its expansion response and makes the effect of radial gradients explicit.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the full shellwise expansion response of a smooth spherical density profile—including distinct radial (H∥) and transverse (H⊥) Hubble rates—is completely fixed by a single top-hat (homogeneous) function. Given the local and enclosed density contrasts, the transverse response and its derivative determine both Hubble rates, with linear and second-order limits being algebraic maps depending only on the growth rate f. An exact equal-age construction provides the nonlinear response without integrating evolution equations, reproducing full ΛLTB profiles to numerical precision, and a cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit achieves maximum errors of 0.3%–0.7%.
AI.motivation: The standard nonlinear density-expansion relation is formulated for a homogeneous spherical top hat with a single local Hubble rate. However, realistic smooth spherical profiles expand anisotropically—differently along and across the radial direction—as a direct signature of radial inhomogeneity. The paper aims to generalize the top-hat relation to capture this anisotropy in a compact, computationally efficient way.
AI.method: The authors show that, for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise expansion response is determined by one top-hat function. Using the local density contrast δ(t,r) and enclosed contrast Δ(t,r), the transverse response and its derivative yield H⊥ and H∥. Linear and second-order limits are algebraic maps depending only on the growth rate f. An exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating an evolution equation, and a derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit uses only f, δ, and Δ.
AI.result: The equal-age construction reconstructs full ΛLTB profiles to numerical precision. Across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations and for a shell in the compensated transition, the maximum relative errors are 0.3% in the transverse response and 0.7% in the radial response for the symbolic fit.
AI.conclusion: This compact formulation separates the production of a density profile from its expansion response, making the effect of radial gradients explicit. It provides a practical, accurate tool for computing shellwise anisotropic expansion in perturbed cosmological density fields without full numerical integration.

title: The solitary star cluster of the Andromeda XXV dwarf spheroidal
comment: Resubmitted to MNRAS after a positive referee report. 11 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables
summary: We present Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys observations of Gep I, a globular cluster (GC) candidate in the low-mass ($M_{\star}\sim 6.5 \times 10^5\,M_{\odot}$) M31 dwarf spheroidal (dSph) satellite Andromeda XXV (And XXV). We confirm the nature of this object and provide the first detailed characterisation of its resolved stellar populations using a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) that reaches 2 magnitudes below the horizontal branch. We compare Gep I's metallicity and distance with those of the surrounding And XXV stellar population, and find them to be strikingly similar, consistent with a physical association between the GC and the dSph. Gep I is very extended ($R_h=24^{+5}_{-4}$ pc) and faint ($M_V = -4.5 \pm 0.2$ mag), similar to the star clusters residing in other low-mass dwarf galaxies. It is characterised by a very low metallicity ($\rm [Fe/H] = -2.4^{+0.3}_{-0.4}\,$dex) and a red horizontal branch morphology, a combination also seen in suspected accreted GCs in the M31 halo and in the Local Group dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 6822. While Gep I is most likely a genuine star cluster, the current data do not exclude the tantalising possibility that it consists of And XXV stars temporarily captured by a dark subhalo orbiting within the dSph's potential well.

AI.tldr: This paper presents HST/ACS observations confirming Gep I as a globular cluster candidate associated with the low-mass M31 dwarf spheroidal galaxy Andromeda XXV. Using a CMD reaching 2 magnitudes below the horizontal branch, the authors find Gep I to be very extended (Rh=24 pc), faint (MV=-4.5), metal-poor ([Fe/H]=-2.4), with a red horizontal branch, matching the surrounding And XXV population in distance and metallicity. They note an alternative exotic possibility that the object could be And XXV stars captured by a dark subhalo.
AI.motivation: To confirm the nature of Gep I, a globular cluster candidate in the low-mass M31 dSph satellite Andromeda XXV, and provide its first detailed characterisation, which is relevant for understanding star cluster formation and evolution in low-mass dwarf galaxies.
AI.method: Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys observations; construction of a colour-magnitude diagram reaching 2 magnitudes below the horizontal branch; comparison of metallicity and distance with the surrounding And XXV stellar population.
AI.result: Gep I is confirmed as an extended (Rh=24 pc) and faint (MV=-4.5) cluster with very low metallicity ([Fe/H]=-2.4) and a red horizontal branch. Its distance and metallicity are strikingly similar to And XXV, consistent with physical association, and its properties resemble clusters in other low-mass dwarf galaxies and suspected accreted GCs in the M31 halo.
AI.conclusion: Gep I is most likely a genuine star cluster associated with And XXV, though current data cannot exclude the possibility that it represents And XXV stars temporarily captured by a dark subhalo within the dSph's potential well.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Constraints on the anisotropic screening and birefringence effects with DR6
comment: 31 pages, 24 figures. To be submitted to ApJ
summary: While we have learned much from recent surveys of the mm-wave sky, many secondary anisotropies of the CMB remain under-explored. We consider two of these here: the anisotropic screening induced by Thomson scattering of CMB photons off free electrons, and cosmic birefringence, the rotation of CMB polarization due to parity-violating physics beyond the standard model. To measure these effects, we apply state-of-the-art estimators for statistical anisotropy to the ACT Data Release 6 CMB data and construct noisy maps and power spectra of both effects. For anisotropic screening, we find no significant detection with the baseline data, and place an upper limit on its power spectrum that is two orders of magnitude above predictions from current reionization models. We obtain evidence for some foreground contamination at one of our frequencies that is consistent with expectations from extragalactic simulations. For our anisotropic birefringence analysis, we also find no detection and place an upper limit on the signal that is consistent with previous analyses. We report a corresponding upper limit on the Chern-Simons coupling term $g_{a γ} < 4.9 \times 10^{-2} / H_\mathrm{I}$, with $H_\mathrm{I}$ the inflationary Hubble scale. These analyses pave the way toward obtaining improved constraints with the next generation of ground-based CMB surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes two under-explored secondary CMB anisotropies—anisotropic screening from Thomson scattering and cosmic birefringence from parity-violating physics—using ACT Data Release 6. No significant detections are found for either effect; upper limits are placed, including a constraint on the Chern-Simons coupling g_aγ < 4.9×10^-2/H_I. The work paves the way for improved constraints with next-generation CMB surveys.
AI.motivation: Recent CMB surveys have greatly advanced our understanding of primary anisotropies, but many secondary anisotropies remain under-explored. This work targets two such signals—anisotropic screening from free-electron Thomson scattering and cosmic birefringence from parity-violating beyond-Standard-Model physics—to probe reionization physics and new fundamental symmetries.
AI.method: The authors apply state-of-the-art statistical anisotropy estimators to ACT Data Release 6 CMB data, constructing noisy maps and power spectra of both anisotropic screening and cosmic birefringence effects.
AI.result: No significant detection of anisotropic screening is found, with an upper limit two orders of magnitude above current reionization model predictions; some foreground contamination at one frequency is observed, consistent with extragalactic simulations. No cosmic birefringence detection is found either; the resulting constraint on the Chern-Simons coupling is g_aγ < 4.9×10^-2/H_I, consistent with previous analyses.
AI.conclusion: The non-detections provide useful upper limits on both secondary anisotropies and establish analysis methodology that will enable improved constraints with next-generation ground-based CMB surveys.

title: HURACAN: A comparison of stellar and interstellar proper motions inside L1688
comment: 19 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables, submitted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The assumption that molecular clouds are kinematically coupled to the young stellar populations forming within them is observationally still poorly constrained. With the transverse component $v_{\textrm{t}}$ of the interstellar medium (ISM) motion being largely unknown, the three-dimensional kinematic state of even the closest clouds remains incomplete. We provide the first direct measurement of the transverse motion of the ISM inside the Ophiuchus cloud L1688 and compare it with the kinematics of the surrounding young stellar populations. The measurement was obtained using intensity-based image registration applied to archival data, allowing us to generate a proper motion field of the studied regions and determine the cloud's bulk motion, $(μ_{α^*},μ_δ)^{\mathrm{ISM}}_{\mathrm{median}}=(-3.0, -24.1)$ mas yr$^{-1}$. This motion differs from the kinematics of the youngest population in Upper Scorpius by $3\pm1$ km s$^{-1}$, highlighting the possibility of a bias when using stars as a proxy for the ISM motion near star-forming regions. By comparing the cloud's motion with that of the youngest stellar population in the region and the B-star Oph S1 located within the cloud, we find that stellar feedback must have dynamically shaped the motion of the ISM over the last few million years. Furthermore, by studying a shell-like ISM structure appearing in L1688, we find evidence suggesting that this object is likely neither a typical Herbig-Haro object nor a supernova remnant, with its origin remaining a mystery. Our results demonstrate that archival and future high-resolution near-infrared observations can and will continue to enable measurements of ISM transverse motions in nearby clouds, opening a new window for studying ISM dynamics that is not accessible when using radial velocities alone.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first direct measurement of the transverse motion of the interstellar medium (ISM) inside the Ophiuchus cloud L1688 using intensity-based image registration on archival near-infrared data. The measured bulk motion differs from the kinematics of the youngest stellar population in Upper Scorpius by 3±1 km/s, suggesting that using stars as proxies for ISM motion can introduce bias. The study indicates stellar feedback dynamically shaped ISM motion over recent million years and reveals a shell-like structure of unknown origin in L1688.
AI.motivation: The three-dimensional kinematic state of molecular clouds remains incomplete because the transverse component of ISM motion is largely unknown. This limits our understanding of whether molecular clouds are kinematically coupled to the young stellar populations forming within them—an assumption that is observationally poorly constrained.
AI.method: The authors used intensity-based image registration applied to archival near-infrared observations to generate a proper motion field of the studied regions in the Ophiuchus cloud L1688, enabling measurement of the cloud's bulk transverse motion. They compared this ISM motion with the kinematics of surrounding young stellar populations and analyzed a shell-like ISM structure in L1688.
AI.result: The measured bulk ISM motion is (μα*, μδ)ISM_median = (-3.0, -24.1) mas yr^-1. This motion differs from the kinematics of the youngest population in Upper Scorpius by 3±1 km/s. The shell-like ISM structure in L1688 is likely neither a typical Herbig-Haro object nor a supernova remnant.
AI.conclusion: Stellar feedback must have dynamically shaped the motion of the ISM over the last few million years, and using stars as proxies for ISM motion near star-forming regions can introduce bias. Archival and future high-resolution near-infrared observations can enable measurements of ISM transverse motions in nearby clouds, opening a new window for studying ISM dynamics beyond radial velocities alone.

title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
comment: Submitted to MNRAS. 18 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables
summary: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of $\sim$0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on shallow, low-resolution photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 132 spectra of red giant and horizontal branch stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure $\rm [Fe/H] =-0.61\pm0.03\,$dex, $v_{\rm los} = 50.9^{+0.8}_{-0.7}\,\rm km \,s^{-1}$, $σ_v = 3.2^{+1.4}_{-1.5}\,\rm km \,s^{-1}$. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a $\sim$3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius ($R_{h}=8.8^{+1.1}_{-1.3}\,$pc), a small flattening ($e=0.14^{+0.12}_{-0.10}$), and low luminosity ($M_{V} = -5.0 \pm 0.4$). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's unique GC system.

AI.tldr: The paper re-examines Fornax 6, a previously suspected globular cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy, using MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode and deep GMOS-S observations. With 132 spectra, the authors confirm Fornax 6 is a distinct chemo-dynamical component with 43 likely members, measuring [Fe/H]=-0.61, v_los=50.9 km/s, and σ_v=3.2 km/s. It is ~3 Gyr old, has irregular morphology, R_h=8.8 pc, low ellipticity, and M_V=-5.0, supporting its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption and making it the youngest, most metal-rich member of Fornax's GC system.
AI.motivation: Fornax 6 was identified as a potential sixth globular cluster in the Fornax dSph galaxy based on shallow photometry and few spectra, but this classification remained uncertain. Since the GC system of Fornax is used to probe dark matter properties, confirming the nature of Fornax 6 is important for understanding the galaxy's cluster population and its implications for dark matter studies.
AI.method: The authors analyzed MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode integral-field observations and deep GMOS-S imaging. They built a sample of 132 spectra of red giant and horizontal branch stars, identifying 43 likely cluster members through chemo-dynamical separation from the field population. They measured metallicity, line-of-sight velocity and velocity dispersion, and used the main-sequence turn-off (observed for the first time) to constrain the age via isochrone fitting, along with structural parameters from photometry.
AI.result: Fornax 6 is confirmed as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with 43 members. Its properties are [Fe/H]=-0.61±0.03 dex, v_los=50.9 km/s, σ_v=3.2 km/s. The MSTO indicates a ~3 Gyr old coeval population. It has an irregular morphology, half-light radius of 8.8 pc, low flattening (e=0.14), and low luminosity (M_V=-5.0). It is the youngest and most metal-rich cluster in Fornax's GC system.
AI.conclusion: The improved characterization supports Fornax 6 being a genuine low-mass globular cluster, likely undergoing tidal disruption. This makes it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's unique globular cluster system, providing new constraints on cluster formation and disruption in dwarf galaxies.

title: Exploring the survivability of higher-order multiple protostellar systems -- The case of VLA1623
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS (Accepted 2026 August 27. Received 2026 August 27; in original form 2025 December 17)
summary: Higher-order protostellar systems ($\geq$3 components) are commonly observed in the early stages of low-mass star formation. A persistent question in star formation and evolution is whether these higher-order protostellar systems survive as gravitationally bound systems or dissolve into binaries over time. We explore this question with a case study of the embedded quadruple protostellar system VLA1623 and its observational constraints, assuming that the components A1, A2, B, and W are gravitationally bound. Using $N$-body simulations, we run a grid of models considering gravity, mass accretion onto protostars, the presence of the protostellar cloud core, and its dispersal. The simulations are integrated over a period of 8 Myr to take into account the evolution from the protostellar phase (Class 0 and I, 1 Myr), through the pre-main sequence (Class II and III, 2 -- 3 Myr), and into the main sequence (4 Myr). Our results show that VLA1623 has a probability of 30% to remain as a gravitationally-bound quadruple system up to 8 Myr from the current state. There is also a 25--30% probability of VLA1623 dissolving into a triple system. This suggests that the dissolution of quadruple protostellar systems contributes to the formation of stable triple (proto)stellar systems. Components A1 and A2 are the most likely to be ejected, while W has a lower probability of being ejected from the system. The stability of VLA1623 depends on a combination of component mass ratios wrt the primary, separations, and eccentricities.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether higher-order protostellar systems survive as bound systems or dissolve into binaries/triples, using the embedded quadruple system VLA1623 as a case study. N-body simulations over 8 Myr incorporating gravity, mass accretion, and cloud core presence/dispersal show a 30% probability of remaining bound as a quadruple and a 25-30% probability of dissolving into a triple system.
AI.motivation: Higher-order protostellar systems (≥3 components) are commonly observed, but a persistent open question is whether they survive as gravitationally bound systems or dissolve into binaries over time. This study aims to address this question through a detailed case study of VLA1623.
AI.method: The authors use N-body simulations with a grid of models that include gravity, mass accretion onto protostars, the presence of the protostellar cloud core, and its dispersal. Simulations are integrated over 8 Myr, spanning the protostellar phase (Class 0/I, ~1 Myr), pre-main sequence (Class II/III, 2-3 Myr), and the main sequence (~4 Myr), assuming components A1, A2, B, and W are gravitationally bound.
AI.result: VLA1623 has a 30% probability of remaining a gravitationally-bound quadruple system up to 8 Myr, and a 25-30% probability of dissolving into a triple system. Components A1 and A2 are the most likely to be ejected, while W has a lower ejection probability. Stability depends on component mass ratios relative to the primary, separations, and eccentricities.
AI.conclusion: The dissolution of quadruple protostellar systems contributes to the formation of stable triple (proto)stellar systems, suggesting that higher-order systems can fragment into lower-order stable configurations over time.

title: $N$-body simulations of the open cluster population in the Milky Way and the impact of GMC encounters
summary: We investigate the population of open clusters in the Solar Neighbourhood and model the effect of encounters with giant molecular clouds (GMCs) over the last 1 Gyr. We combine a Galactic model with $N$-body simulations of 20692 unique clusters in the mass range $[50-24000]$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$. Each cluster is simulated twice: with and without tidal forces from the GMCs. We find that an initial cluster mass function truncated at $\sim 9000$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ best reproduces the observed mass function evolution. For the age function, the observations show a decline in clusters for ages older than $\sim 1$ Myr, whereas our simulated clusters show a decline after $\sim 50$ Myr. The observed early disruption suggests that some clusters form supervirial, whereas our simulated clusters are created in virial equilibrium. Low-mass ($<600 \, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) clusters are most sensitive to GMC encounters, which accelerate their disruption in the first $\sim 200$ Myr. After $\sim 500$ Myr, the impact of GMCs becomes irrelevant since the clusters will have been destroyed regardless of whether they experience GMC encounters or not. The survival of intermediate-mass ($600-6000\, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) clusters is significantly reduced by GMCs at ages up to 1 Gyr. High-mass ($>6000 \, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) clusters survive to 1 Gyr with minimal disruption with or without GMCs. We find that clusters that have had strong GMC encounters within the last $20$ Myr should have tidal tails that are randomly orientated with respect to the Galactic centre.

AI.tldr: This paper models the population of open clusters in the Solar Neighbourhood over the last 1 Gyr, combining Galactic models with N-body simulations of 20,692 clusters (50–24,000 M☉), each simulated with and without GMC tidal forces. The best match to observed mass function evolution requires an initial cluster mass function truncated at ~9000 M☉. Observed clusters are disrupted earlier (~1 Myr) than simulated ones (~50 Myr), suggesting supervirial formation. Low-mass clusters (<600 M☉) are most sensitive to GMC encounters within the first 200 Myr; intermediate-mass clusters (600–6000 M☉) are affected up to 1 Gyr; high-mass clusters (>6000 M☉) survive with minimal disruption. Clusters with strong GMC encounters in the last 20 Myr should have randomly oriented tidal tails relative to the Galactic centre.
AI.motivation: To understand how encounters with giant molecular clouds (GMCs) affect the population, disruption, and evolution of open clusters in the Solar Neighbourhood over the past 1 Gyr, and to reconcile simulated cluster populations with observed mass and age functions.
AI.method: Combines a Galactic model with N-body simulations of 20,692 unique open clusters spanning masses 50–24,000 M☉. Each cluster is simulated twice—once with GMC tidal forces and once without—to isolate the effects of GMC encounters. Cluster populations are compared with observed mass and age functions.
AI.result: An initial cluster mass function truncated at ~9000 M☉ best reproduces observed mass function evolution. Simulated clusters survive until ~50 Myr before declining, whereas observed clusters decline after ~1 Myr, implying supervirial cluster formation. Low-mass clusters (<600 M☉) are most vulnerable to GMC disruption within the first 200 Myr; GMC effects become negligible after ~500 Myr for these clusters. Intermediate-mass clusters (600–6000 M☉) experience significantly reduced survival up to 1 Gyr due to GMCs, while high-mass clusters (>6000 M☉) survive with minimal disruption either way. Clusters with strong GMC encounters within the last 20 Myr should exhibit randomly oriented tidal tails with respect to the Galactic centre.
AI.conclusion: GMC encounters play a mass-dependent role in open cluster disruption, most strongly affecting low-mass clusters early in their lifetimes and intermediate-mass clusters over longer timescales. The discrepancy between observed and simulated disruption timescales points to supervirial formation in real clusters, and strong recent GMC encounters leave observable signatures in the orientation of tidal tails.

title: Non-isothermal vertical distribution functions for the Milky Way
summary: The vertical structure of our Galaxy has commonly been assumed to follow a pseudo-isothermal distribution. However, there is no \textit{a priori} reason to expect this form to arise from scattering by giant molecular clouds (GMCs), since GMCs are confined to a narrow layer around the Galactic midplane and therefore do not randomise stars uniformly in vertical phase space. We first present a simple statistical argument to derive a new vertical distribution function (DF), in the limiting case of a razor-thin distribution of GMCs, which admits an extra factor of ${J_z}^{-α}$, where $α>0$ and varies for different potentials. In light of this, we revisit the diffusion coefficients for vertical heating from the mechanics of two-body scattering, in a more realistic, extended distribution of GMCs. The resulting drift and diffusion coefficients are strongly non-linear in $v_z$, particularly at low relative velocities, where the effective range of weak, local encounters can vanish. We determine stationary solutions, and also numerically solve the orbit-averaged Fokker--Planck equation with time-dependent coefficients. We find, in both cases, a vertical action distribution that deviates from that of the pseudo-isothermal case, and propose a new, family of vertical DFs that generalise the pseudo-isothermal form. We find the two primary agents of non-isothermality are: (i) a GMC distribution confined near the midplane, and (ii) the fact that the Coulomb logarithm, $Λ$ is strongly velocity-dependent at small velocities, and cannot be treated as a constant, contrary to the commonly adopted assumption.

Using a statistical argument for a razor-thin GMC distribution, the authors derive a new vertical distribution function with an extra J_z^-α factor. They revisit two-body scattering diffusion coefficients for vertical heating and solve the orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck equation, finding that the vertical action distribution deviates from pseudo-isothermal. They propose a generalized family of vertical DFs and identify two causes of non-isothermality: GMCs confined near the midplane and a velocity-dependent Coulomb logarithm at small velocities.
AI.motivation: The pseudo-isothermal vertical distribution is widely assumed for the Galactic disk, yet there is no physical justification that scattering by GMCs (confined to a narrow midplane layer) should produce such a form, since GMCs do not randomise stars uniformly in vertical phase space.
AI.method: The authors (i) derive a new vertical DF via a statistical argument in the razor-thin GMC limit, giving an extra factor of J_z^-α; (ii) compute drift and diffusion coefficients from two-body scattering mechanics with an extended GMC distribution; and (iii) solve both stationary solutions and numerically solve the time-dependent orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck equation.

Both stationary and time-dependent solutions yield vertical action distributions that deviate from the pseudo-isothermal form. A new family of generalized vertical DFs is proposed.

title: LightCube: A Parsec-Resolution 3D Model of the Local Far-Ultraviolet Interstellar Radiation Field
summary: We present a three-dimensional model of the local interstellar radiation field (ISRF) in the ultraviolet (UV). Using UV flux measurements from the TD1 catalog and stellar distances from Gaia and Hipparcos, we construct a catalog of stars that we expect to dominate the UV flux in the nearby Galaxy. We use the radiative transfer code DIRTY to model the propagation of photons from these stars through a 3D dust map, including the effects of scattering and absorption. The result is LightCube, a model of the ultraviolet ISRF out to 1.25 kpc from the Sun, with a maximum linear resolution of 1 pc. We model the ISRF in the four TD1 bands (1565 A, 1965 A, 2365 A, and 2740 A), as well as a single value for the full FUV range, and calculate the ISRF at the Sun to be 5.65$\times$10$^{-14}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ from 912 A to 2000 A. The modeled ISRF is quite variable, with more than an order of magnitude variation seen in dense regions, and about half that in lower density regions. By comparing LightCube to an estimate of the 3D distribution of total-to-selective extinction ratio, $R_V$, we find a positive correlation between UV flux and $R_V$ in regions of low UV radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents LightCube, a 3D model of the local interstellar radiation field (ISRF) in the ultraviolet, constructed using TD1 catalog UV flux measurements, Gaia/Hipparcos stellar distances, and the DIRTY radiative transfer code to propagate photons through a 3D dust map. The model covers out to 1.25 kpc from the Sun with up to 1 pc resolution, finding the ISRF at the Sun to be 5.65×10^-14 erg cm^-3 over 912-2000 Å, showing significant variability, and revealing a positive correlation between UV flux and the total-to-selective extinction ratio R_V in low-UV regions.
AI.motivation: To construct a detailed 3D model of the ultraviolet interstellar radiation field in the local Galaxy, which is essential for understanding dust properties, star formation, and interstellar medium processes, but previously lacked high-resolution three-dimensional treatment incorporating realistic dust scattering and absorption.
AI.method: Constructs a catalog of UV-dominant stars using TD1 UV flux measurements and Gaia/Hipparcos distances, then uses the radiative transfer code DIRTY to propagate stellar photons through a 3D dust map accounting for scattering and absorption, producing the LightCube model at 1 pc resolution out to 1.25 kpc in four TD1 bands (1565, 1965, 2365, 2740 Å) plus a full FUV value.
AI.result: The ISRF at the Sun is calculated to be 5.65×10^-14 erg cm^-3 from 912-2000 Å. The modeled ISRF varies by more than an order of magnitude in dense regions and about half that in lower density regions. A positive correlation between UV flux and R_V is found in regions of low UV radiation.
AI.conclusion: The LightCube model provides a high-resolution, fully three-dimensional treatment of the UV ISRF in the local Galaxy, demonstrating substantial spatial variability driven by dust geometry and stellar distribution, and suggesting a relationship between UV radiation field strength and dust grain properties as traced by R_V.

title: Map of the Interstellar Continuum FUV Field within 800 Parsecs
summary: The far-ultraviolet (FUV) field, consisting of photons with energies between 6 and 13.6 electron volts, plays an important role in the chemical and thermodynamical evolution of the interstellar medium. FUV continuum radiation is produced by bright stars in the galaxy and absorbed by interstellar dust. We used newly available maps of the dust distribution, in conjunction with catalogs of stellar positions and spectra, to create a map of the stellar FUV field within 800 parsecs of the Earth. The map shows a total FUV intensity in the solar neighborhood in line with existing measurements (0.7 times the Draine field), but substantial point-to-point fluctuations exist. Near the Galactic midplane, the FUV intensity decreases with increasing gas density up to a density of approximately 10 hydrogen atoms per cm$^3$, due to absorption of light by dust. Between 10 and 50 hydrogen atoms per cm$^3$ the UV field increases again, due to a positive correlation between high density gas and young hot stars. We find that the spectrum is generally harder where the UV field is higher, and softer in regions where dust extinction is more important. The resulting map, as well as our catalog of derived stellar properties, are both available for download for those wishing to study a nearby region of the ISM.

The map shows a total FUV intensity consistent with prior measurements (0.7 Draine field) but with significant spatial fluctuations, revealing complex relationships between FUV intensity, gas density, and dust extinction.

Existing measurements only provide average values, obscuring local variations.
AI.method: The authors combined newly available dust distribution maps with catalogs of stellar positions and spectra to compute and map the stellar FUV field within 800 parsecs of Earth.
